question: Will Singapore's 24-hour PSI reach the Unhealthy band (101 or higher) in at least one region on September 17 or 18, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Reference class (2-day windows in mid/late September of years where a transboundary haze episode had already pushed Singapore PSI into Unhealthy in early September: 2015, 2019, 2023-Oct analog, 2006) implies roughly 0.55. Adjusting up: intensifying El Nino with below-normal regional rainfall, SW Monsoon and SE/S transport winds persisting to early October, 17-18 Sep sitting in the climatological haze peak, NEA's own forecast band explicitly including Low Unhealthy and its ~two-week persistence statement, peat fires that smoulder after hotspots fade, and an unusually generous criterion (any 1 of 5 regions, any hourly update, 2 days) that only needs Central — which ran 20-35 points above the lowest region on 4-5 Sep — to touch 101 once. Adjusting down: the last two days were clearly Moderate (max 92), Riau/Jambi are at ~zero hotspots so the nearest Sumatran source is quiescent, Kalimantan counts fell from their late-August peak under suppression and cloud seeding with showers forecast there, and 10-11 days exceeds skillful wind/rain forecast range. Decomposed: P(episode still Unhealthy-capable on 17-18 Sep) ~0.80 x P(hit over a correlated 2-day window | capable) ~0.68, plus a small residual, gives ~0.56; nudged to 0.58 for El Nino intensification into the seasonal peak. No market exists on this contract.

calls.reference_class: Two-day windows in mid-to-late September in years where transboundary haze had already produced an Unhealthy (>=101) regional 24-hr PSI reading in Singapore during the first week of September, under dry-season/El Nino conditions (1997, 2006, 2014, 2015, 2019, 2023-Oct analog)

calls.reasoning: Base rate for a random 2-day September window in Singapore is ~13% (≈30 Unhealthy Sept days across 2013-2025, concentrated in 2015 and 2019), but conditioning dominates: an episode is already underway (Sep 4-6 all crossed 101, Central peaking 123), a strengthening super El Niño (>90% very strong in NH fall), the Sept-Oct Indonesian fire-season peak, 15,652 Kalimantan+Sumatra hotspots YTD with 1,400+/day in West/Central Kalimantan by Sep 1, below-normal rainfall forecast through October, and a weak MJO with no Maritime-Continent rain pulse until ~Sep 25-27 mean no obvious clearing mechanism before the window. The resolution instrument is highly permissive — any of 5 regions at any of ~48 hourly updates on a rolling 24-hr mean, with the threshold sitting mid-band in the observed 90-125 oscillation. Chief counterweight: dense regional smoke was present over Sumatra/Kalimantan on most days from ~Aug 21 yet produced zero Singapore Unhealthy readings until Sep 4, proving regional severity alone is insufficient without southerly wind alignment; the current episode is already decaying (Sep 7 max 92) and Sep 17-18 is ~10 days beyond forecast skill, so day-specific wind alignment is close to a coin flip conditional on the regime. No prediction market prices this event on any venue I checked (Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi, bookmakers), so there is no anchor to blend against. Roughly 0.90 that the fire/dry regime persists to the window, times ~0.6 that exposure aligns on at least one of the two days.

calls.reasoning: Fire source and transport regime are near seasonal peak and forecast to persist: El Nino peaking in September, ASMC Alert Level 3 for southern ASEAN, ~7,400 hotspots in West Kalimantan, and Indonesia's forestry minister stating natural rainfall may not return until early October; MJO is weak/suppressed over the Maritime Continent through mid-September. Base rate anchor: across Septembers with an already-active Singapore haze episode (1997, 2006, 2014, 2015, 2019, 2023), roughly half of 2-day windows ~10-14 days post-onset contained a regional 24-hr PSI >=101 - high in strong-El Nino years (2015 sustained Unhealthy for weeks), low in weaker years (2019 ended with rain on day 10-11; 2023 faded within days). Adjusting up: 2026 matches the strong-El Nino template, and the resolution bar is generous (any of 5 regions, any hourly update, over 48 hours), with even the current Moderate lull days peaking at 92-95, ~8 points below threshold. Adjusting down: the last two days (6-7 Sep) were entirely Moderate, showing wind/transport gates the outcome day-to-day; Indonesia has surged cloud seeding, water bombing and 1,000 extra personnel; and the window is 9-11 days out, so regime persistence is genuinely uncertain. Direct empirical anchor from the current episode: 2 of 3 rolling 2-day windows over 4-7 Sep contained a >=101 reading.

- BMKG issued an extreme-weather warning for medium-to-heavy rainfall in Aceh, North Sumatra, North Kalimantan and South Sulawesi for 3-5 Sep 2026, showing rain events do occur in-season (though these provinces are mostly north of the main plume source).
- The 2019 precedent shows episodes are bursty: multi-day Moderate gaps occurred between Unhealthy bursts within the same advisory period.

calls.reference_class: Two-consecutive-day windows inside an active NEA-advisory transboundary haze episode in Singapore during a strong El Nino / peak dry season (Sep 2014, Sep-Oct 2015, Sep 2019, Oct 2023), asking whether any regional 24-h PSI reached >=101

calls.reasoning: Episode onset 4 Sep; 17-18 Sep is day 13-14 post-onset, ~10 days beyond any skillful wind/rain forecast. Verified episode record is 2 of 4 days at 101+ (the disputed '103 on 6 Sep' was actually Central at 7pm on 5 Sep). Mixture: ~55% weight on the 1997/2015 template (super El Nino + positive IOD, no rain until October, ASMC Level-3 alert, South Sumatra hotspot surge to 1,583 - the classic Singapore-relevant source under SW monsoon, MJO pulse not until ~25-27 Sep) at ~0.85, and ~45% on the 2019/2023 bursty template at ~0.28 (2019: 6 Unhealthy days in 30). That yields ~0.59; nudged to 0.62 because the criterion is a max over ~240 region-hours of a rolling mean while quoted lull maxima (92-93) sit only ~9 points below threshold, so observed crossing days are likely undercounted. Held down by: national hotspot counts easing (805 on 2 Sep to 674 on 6 Sep), Riau/Jambi at zero, an active suppression campaign, and the demonstration that 21 Aug-3 Sep dense regional smoke produced no Singapore Unhealthy reading at all.
calls.reconciliation: Four runs spanned 0.56-0.66. I ran five targeted checks on the disputed premises. (1) Run 2's '6 Sep: 103 recorded' is wrong - the 103 was Central at 7pm on 5 Sep; 6 Sep ran 72-87, all Moderate. Verified episode rate is 2 of 4 days, not 3 of 4, which cuts against the more bullish runs. (2) Hotspot magnitude settled: Indonesian high-confidence counts were 805 nationally on 2 Sep and 674 on 6 Sep, with BMKG at Kalbar 907 / Kalteng 671. Run 3's 'West Kalimantan 7,377 in one day' is a cumulative-season figure and the Background's 'tens of thousands' is not a daily count - daily fire activity is flat-to-easing, not exploding. (3) Run 1 and Run 4 were both partly right on Sumatra and the resolution favours Run 4's read: Riau and Jambi are at zero hotspots, but BMKG detected a surge of 2,671 across Sumatra with 1,583 in South Sumatra - the source province that drove the 2015 Singapore episode under southwest-monsoon flow. This upgrades Run 1's 'the Sumatran source is quiescent'. (4) Confirmed empty, as all runs reported: NEA's advisory index returned no content and the ASMC subseasonal outlook page 404'd; no published forecast covers 17-18 Sep. Contemporaneous reporting does corroborate the super-El-Nino framing. (5) I did no independent market check; all four runs found no contract on Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi or with bookmakers, and Run 3 noted Kalshi's endpoint returned HTTP 429 so it is unverified rather than confirmed absent. There is no crowd anchor. The remaining dispute - whether day 13-14 belongs to the 2015 template or the 2019/2023 template - is pure judgment that no available evidence breaks at a 10-day lead; I weight it ~55/45 toward the 2015 template on the El Nino/IOD configuration and the October rain timing, and state that as a bet, not a finding. I did not average the runs: the factual corrections cut both ways (crossing rate down, Sumatran source up) and my 0.62 comes from the mixture (~0.59) plus an upward adjustment for the permissiveness of the instrument - a max over ~240 region-hours of a rolling 24-hour mean, with quoted lull maxima only ~9 index points below the threshold, meaning reported daily maxima are systematically biased low.

disagreements.verdict: Resolved against Run 2: the 103 was Central at 7pm on 5 Sep; 6 Sep ranged 72-87. Episode crossing record is 2 of 4 days.

disagreements.verdict: Resolved: 805 high-confidence nationally on 2 Sep, 674 on 6 Sep; BMKG Kalbar 907 / Kalteng 671. Run 3's 7,377 is cumulative-season; the Background figure is not a daily count.

disagreements.claim: The Sumatran source is quiescent (Riau 0, Jambi 0-4) vs active (South Sumatra 1,000+)
disagreements.verdict: Both hold: Riau and Jambi are at zero, but BMKG reported a 2,671-hotspot surge across Sumatra with 1,583 in South Sumatra - the 2015-template source for Singapore. Favours Run 4's read over Run 1's.

disagreements.claim: A published meteorological outlook covering 17-18 Sep exists
disagreements.verdict: Confirmed absent. NEA's advisory index returned no content and ASMC's subseasonal outlook page 404'd; MSS's second-fortnight outlook was unpublished as of 7 Sep.

disagreements.claim: Day 13-14 post-onset follows the 2015 template (episode persists for weeks) or the 2019/2023 template (bursty, ends by ~day 10)
disagreements.verdict: Unbreakable at a 10-day lead - no forecast has skill here. Weighted ~55/45 toward the 2015 template on the El Nino + positive IOD configuration and the October rain timing; stated as a bet, not a finding.

disagreements.claim: How much the permissive criterion (5 regions x ~48 hourly updates of a rolling mean) is worth
disagreements.verdict: Resolved upward: quoted lull maxima of 92-93 are single-hour snapshots, so the true max over ~240 region-hours is biased low and the observed 2-of-4 likely undercounts. This is the reason 0.62 sits above the 0.59 the mixture alone implies.

disagreements.claim: A prediction market prices this event
disagreements.verdict: None found by any run on Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi or with bookmakers; Kalshi unverified due to an HTTP 429. No crowd anchor to blend against.

calls.reference_class: 2-day windows falling 12-15 days after onset of an NEA-advisory transboundary haze episode in Singapore, in Indonesian fire seasons of the last three decades (1997, 2006, 2013, 2014, 2015, 2019, Oct 2023)
